issue.title: fix(cache): increase max connections per host to improve performance
issue.body:
## Description

Thumbnails in the user profile sometimes didn’t load because they got stuck, causing the blurhash to display forever. With darker videos especially, this looked like a visual glitch or as if something was broken.

This PR fixes the issue so thumbnails now load completely and correctly by using `VineCacheImage`.


**Related Issue:** Closes #4330

issue.body:
### What would you like?

Being able to mention a user directly in the text overlay.  like "@rabble dancing in their @rabble-cat suit at @burningman" 

### How would this be useful for you?

To tag the user name of a place or person for other to go to their account and follow: https://divine.video/video/6de259e876f8a13edca455f54fc7f60dde66d597df6f61791928f3f444e0104a?source=profile&pubkey=076c979382b90f5d3a2b21f95e1ee86b6033f14c92e79b7fad3fe1f1073f4886&index=7  

### When would you use this?

Here i wanted to tag the barista who does latte art workshops and the coffee shop. 
When I wanto let folks know of a place where i recorded this so they can visit. or when they should follow a someone doing interesting stuff.

issue.title: fix(safety): honor current adult content settings for 18+ playback
issue.body:
## Summary
- make 18+ playback follow the current per-category adult content settings instead of the legacy `adult_content_preference` flag
- derive a single playback policy from the adult label filters so mixed settings fall back to warn instead of blocking playback outright
- add regression coverage for the media auth interceptor and the new adult playback preference aggregation

## Testing
- `flutter test test/services/media_auth_interceptor_test.dart test/services/media_auth_interceptor_preference_test.dart test/services/content_filter_service_test.dart`
- `flutter analyze lib/services/content_filter_service.dart lib/services/media_auth_interceptor.dart lib/providers/app_providers.dart test/services/media_auth_interceptor_test.dart test/services/media_auth_interceptor_preference_test.dart test/services/content_filter_service_test.dart`

Closes #4348

issue.title: task: optional prefetch duration cap with setClips file-first playback in InfiniteVideoFeed
issue.body:
## What would you like?

An optional `prefetchDuration` parameter (`Duration?`, default `null`) on `InfiniteVideoFeed` that limits disk prefetching to the first N seconds of each video. When playback begins for a prefetched video the player uses `setClips` to stitch together:

1. **Clip 1** – `file:///.../cached-segment` from `0 ms` to `prefetchDuration` (plays instantly from disk)
2. **Clip 2** – the network URL from `prefetchDuration` onwards (streams the remainder from network)

When `prefetchDuration` is `null` (default) behaviour is unchanged: full file prefetch, played from disk.

## How would this be useful for you?

Currently `InfiniteVideoFeed` downloads entire video files before marking them as prefetched. For 6.3 s clips at 1080p this can be 6-10 MB per video just to warm the buffer. On cellular this burns data and can actually slow down the currently-playing video.

A 2-second prefetch cap gives the same instant-start feel on swipe (no buffering spinner) while downloading only ~2–5 MB. The network stream picks up seamlessly after those 2 seconds.

## When would you use this?

Pass `prefetchDuration: const Duration(seconds: 2)` wherever the feed is constructed for cellular or bandwidth-conscious contexts. Callers can vary the value based on `BandwidthTrackerService` quality, or leave it `null` for Wi-Fi / unlimited scenarios.

## Anything else?

**Affected files / implementation sketch:**

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `InfiniteVideoFeed` (widget) | Add `final Duration? prefetchDuration` parameter, thread through to `DiskPrefetcher` |
| `DiskPrefetcher` | Accept `maxDuration`; stop the `MediaCacheManager` download after N seconds of content |
| `MediaCacheManager` | May need a `downloadPartial` / byte-range API if not already present |
| `_initController` | When `prefetchDuration != null` and a partial file is cached: call `setClips([VideoClip.file(path, endMs: N), VideoClip.network(url, startMs: N)])` instead of `setSource(VideoClip.file(path))` |

**Prior art already in place:**
- `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.kt` already supports multi-clip stitching via `setClips` (array of `{uri, startMs, endMs}`).
- `_initController` already does file-first → `registerPrestart(networkSources)` for corruption failover — the new path extends this pattern.
- `BandwidthTrackerService.shouldUseHighQuality` is an existing signal for bandwidth-aware decisions.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `InfiniteVideoFeed` accepts optional `prefetchDuration` (default `null`)
- [ ] When `null`: existing behaviour unchanged, all current tests pass
- [ ] When set: `DiskPrefetcher` caps the download to the requested duration of video content
- [ ] `_initController` issues `setClips([file 0→N, network N→end])` for a capped prefetch hit
- [ ] If the partial file is missing or corrupt, fallback to plain network playback still works
- [ ] Unit tests for `DiskPrefetcher` partial-download behaviour
- [ ] Widget / integration test verifying the `setClips` path is exercised when `prefetchDuration` is set

issue.title: task(divine_video_player): add preloadDurationMs parameter for duration-limited preloading
issue.body:
## Context

`DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` is currently called only in `video_recorder_provider.dart` (not in `InfiniteVideoFeed`). The Infinite Feed uses a separate two-track preloading strategy:

1. **`DiskPrefetcher`** — downloads video files to disk via `MediaCacheManager`
2. **`_initController(index ± 1)`** — creates full `DivineVideoPlayerController` instances (ExoPlayer/AVPlayer) for adjacent feed items

`DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` is a lightweight "metadata + first-bytes" preload that is used by the **recorder flow** (in `video_recorder_provider.dart`) to warm up the next clip before it is needed for playback.

> Videos in this app are **max 6.3 seconds long**.

## Problem

On Android, `preload()` creates an ExoPlayer with a default `DefaultLoadControl` (~50 s max buffer), which causes it to buffer far more data than necessary for a 6.3 s clip. On iOS/macOS the current implementation is metadata-only (`AVURLAsset.loadValuesAsynchronously(forKeys: ["duration", "tracks"])`) and performs no actual byte buffering at all.

## Goal

Add an optional `preloadDurationMs` parameter to `DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` so callers can cap how many milliseconds of media are buffered ahead of time.

- `null` (default) → existing behaviour (no change for current callers)
- e.g. `2000` → buffer at most 2 s of the clip

## Affected files

### Dart API
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_controller.dart`
  - Add `{int? preloadDurationMs}` to `static Future<void> preload(List<VideoClip> clips, {int? preloadDurationMs})`
  - Pass value in the method-channel args map when non-null

### Android

issue.title: task(divine_video_player): add preloadDurationMs parameter for duration-limited preloading
issue.body:
## Context

`DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` is currently called only in `video_recorder_provider.dart` (not in `InfiniteVideoFeed`). The Infinite Feed uses a separate two-track preloading strategy:

1. **`DiskPrefetcher`** — downloads video files to disk via `MediaCacheManager`
2. **`_initController(index ± 1)`** — creates full `DivineVideoPlayerController` instances (ExoPlayer/AVPlayer) for adjacent feed items

`DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` is a lightweight "metadata + first-bytes" preload that is used by the **recorder flow** (in `video_recorder_provider.dart`) to warm up the next clip before it is needed for playback.

> Videos in this app are **max 6.3 seconds long**.

## Problem

On Android, `preload()` creates an ExoPlayer with a default `DefaultLoadControl` (~50 s max buffer), which causes it to buffer far more data than necessary for a 6.3 s clip. On iOS/macOS the current implementation is metadata-only (`AVURLAsset.loadValuesAsynchronously(forKeys: ["duration", "tracks"])`) and performs no actual byte buffering at all.

## Goal

Add an optional `preloadDurationMs` parameter to `DivineVideoPlayerController.preload()` so callers can cap how many milliseconds of media are buffered ahead of time.

- `null` (default) → existing behaviour (no change for current callers)
- e.g. `2000` → buffer at most 2 s of the clip

## Affected files

### Dart API
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_controller.dart`
  - Add `{int? preloadDurationMs}` to `static Future<void> preload(List<VideoClip> clips, {int? preloadDurationMs})`
  - Pass value in the method-channel args map when non-null

### Android
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/example/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.kt`
  - In `handlePreload()`: when `preloadDurationMs` is present, build `DefaultLoadControl` with `setBufferDurationsMs(durationMs, durationMs, durationMs, durationMs / 2)` before constructing ExoPlayer

### iOS
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/ios/Classes/DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.swift`
  - When `preloadDurationMs` is set: switch from metadata-only `AVURLAsset.loadValuesAsynchronously` to `AVPlayerItem(url:)` + `item.preferredForwardBufferDuration = Double(preloadDurationMs) / 1000.0` + `AVPlayer(playerItem:)`
  - When absent: keep current metadata-only path

### macOS
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/macos/Classes/DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.swift`
  - Same change as iOS

## Tests

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/test/src/divine_video_player_controller_test.dart`
  - Add test: `preload` with `preloadDurationMs` sends correct args on the method channel
  - Add test: `preload` without `preloadDurationMs` sends args without the key (backwards compat)

## Out of scope

`InfiniteVideoFeed` preloading is handled by `DiskPrefetcher` + `_initController` and is **not** affected by this change.

comment.body:
I think this still leaves a profile-feed moderation hole.

`ProfileFeed` fetches profile videos directly from Funnelcake and then filters them through `VideoEventService.filterVideoList` (`mobile/lib/providers/profile_feed_provider.dart`). That path does not use `createNsfwFilter`.

Inside `VideoEventService.filterVideoList`, `video.moderationLabels` are checked with `service.getPreferenceForLabels(modLabels)`. `getPreferenceForLabels` skips labels that are not in `ContentLabel` and falls back to `show`, so an ML/server moderation label the client does not recognize can pass through instead of being hidden.

That looks relevant to the report here because Funnelcake/model tests already normalize `"sexual content"` to `"sexual-content"`, while the UI enum recognizes `sexual`, not `sexual-content`. So suggestive/twerking content labeled `sexual-content` can still appear on profile feeds even when adult categories are locked to hide in Content Filters.

The repository path already has the safer behavior in `createNsfwFilter`: unknown ML moderation labels force-hide. Can we add coverage for `VideoEventService.filterVideoList` with something like `moderationLabels: ['sexual-content']` or another unknown ML label, and make this path match the conservative ML-label hide behavior?

-## Engineering Guardrails
+## Scope Discipline
 
-- Prefer `UI -> BLoC/Cubit -> Repository -> Client` for new feature work.
-- Constructor injection over hidden singletons.
-- No arbitrary `Future.delayed()` in app logic.
-- Never truncate Nostr IDs in code, logs, analytics, or tests.
-- Reuse `divine_ui` components and `VineTheme` instead of one-off styling.
-- Keep public copy direct, human, and aligned with the brand guidelines.
+Keep PRs focused and reviewable.
 
-## Pull Requests
+Do:
 
-- Use a Conventional Commit PR title, for example `feat(settings): split settings into sub-screens`.
+- Change only what is required for the agreed task.
 - Stage only task-related files.
+- Keep dependency changes justified and narrow.
+- Split truly independent work into separate PRs targeting `main`.
+
+Do not:
+
+- Mix feature work with unrelated cleanup or version bumps.
+- Add speculative architecture while solving a smaller problem.
+- Land partial work with TODOs instead of finishing or scoping down.
+- Introduce new technical debt with the expectation that maintainers will clean
+  it up later.
+- Leave generated files stale.
+- Leave the branch dirty at handoff.
+
+## Pull Requests
+
+Requirements:
+
+- Use a Conventional Commit PR title such as
+  `feat(settings): split settings into sub-screens`.
+- Make sure the PR title is semantic when the PR is opened. Editing the title
+  later does not reliably retrigger all checks.
+- Target `main`.
+- Fill out `.github/pull_request_template.md` completely, including the
+  description, related issue, and type-of-change checklist.
+- Include a clear description of what changed, what is out of scope, and how

comment.body:
Thanks, this is helpful context @hm21.

My understanding is that there are really two separate concerns here:

1. the player / transport side, where the move away from MediaKit and toward the native player with HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 already seems to improve real-world playback behavior, especially on weak connections
2. the caching / preload strategy side, where we still have a more waterfall-style approach than we want

That distinction makes sense to me, and from a tech-debt perspective I'd rather we keep those separated than let this turn into one broad “video loading is slow” bucket.

If the native player migration is already addressing the first part, then the “preload the first 1–2 seconds first, then continue only if the user keeps watching” idea sounds like a distinct optimization task and probably should be tracked separately under the broader caching/data-foundation work rather than folded ambiguously into this issue.

I'm deferring to you on the implementation details, but the separation you're drawing here makes sense to me.

issue.title: fix(security): remove BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth PKCE verifier and request body
issue.body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Critical

## Problem
BYOK registration embeds the user nsec into the PKCE verifier and posts the nsec to Keycast during headless registration.

## Evidence
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart:9-12 appends .$nsec to the PKCE verifier.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:155-171 accepts optional nsec and uses it in verifier generation.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:280-286 derives BYOK pubkey and generates verifier with nsec.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:299-301 puts nsec into the registration request body.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:81-95 exports local nsec and passes it into registration.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:117-122 calls headlessRegister(... nsec: nsec ...).

## Impact
BYOK/private key material leaves local storage and is also carried in the PKCE verifier, breaking the expected local-key custody boundary.

## Recommended fix
Never send or embed nsec. Use a local proof-of-possession challenge signed by the key, or send only byok_pubkey and a signature over server-provided nonce/session data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No nsec appears in OAuth URL, PKCE verifier, persisted pending verification, request body, logs, or tests.
- [ ] Server receives only public key plus proof.
- [ ] BYOK registration still binds the account to the intended Nostr pubkey.
- [ ] Tests assert verifier does not contain nsec1.

## Related issues
Adjacent: #969, #3066, #3270.

comment.body:
Thanks for laying this out explicitly @realmeylisdev

My understanding is:

`#3784` does successfully remove the current security problem by stopping the user's `nsec` from leaving the device. That addresses the leak itself, which I agree is important and necessary.

My understanding of the tradeoff, though, is that `Approach A` is not just “the same BYOK flow, but safer.” It closes the leak by temporarily changing what the secure-account / BYOK path does in practice. Today that flow preserves the user's existing identity in Keycast-managed custody. Under `Approach A`, that identity-preservation behavior is intentionally not preserved until the Phase 2 server/mobile work lands.

That matters to me because I care not just about eliminating existing tech debt, but also about not introducing new debt as part of the fix. From that lens, `Approach A` removes one critical form of debt, but it does so by creating another knowingly temporary state that depends on follow-up work to restore the intended contract. I don't love that trade.

So my read is:

- `Approach A`: remove the leak now, but accept a temporary BYOK/product-contract regression and a new follow-up dependency.
- `Approach B`: keep the PR in draft until the Phase 2 path is ready, so we remove the leak without redefining the feature in the interim.

On that basis, I'm `Approach B`.

That said, I'm deferring to @dcadenas and @rabble on the final call here, since they have the deepest context on the intended Keycast/BYOK contract and the acceptable security/product tradeoff. If they decide this needs to be treated as an emergency exception, I'm fine aligning to that explicitly, but my preference is still `Approach B`.

comment.body:
@NotThatKindOfDrLiz Until now we still mainly use MediaKit, which only runs with HTTP/1. The switch to the new native video player also introduces HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support.

Since I’m currently in Vietnam in a remote village from my wife’s family with a pretty bad internet connection, I can clearly see the difference. With MediaKit it’s basically impossible for me to watch any video without first seeing a loading indicator. However, with the native video player I can scroll through the feed with mostly no loading spinner at all, so HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 already seem to be a huge improvement.

That said, there’s still room for improvement because the caching system is not 100% optimal yet. Right now it behaves more like a waterfall approach where it loads the full video step by step. That’s not ideal for users with poor internet connections.

A better approach would probably be to first preload only the first 1–2 seconds of a video instantly instead of trying to cache the full video immediately. Then the remaining parts could continue loading from the network only if the user actually keeps watching the video.

I think this should probably be the next optimization step, but maybe it makes sense to create a separate task for that?

issue.title: epic(data-foundation): unify caching, persistence, and platform dependency strategy
issue.body:
## Summary

Caching, persistence, and platform dependency choices are currently fragmented across multiple storage backends, cache policies, and ownership models. This should be tracked as one coordinated foundation epic instead of several disconnected discussion issues.

This issue is the source of truth for data foundation work around caching, persistence, storage strategy, and shared dependency ownership.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- multiple cache systems with different TTL and invalidation rules
- overlapping persistent storage backends
- unclear ownership of platform/dependency decisions
- weak consistency around schema/versioning and long-term storage strategy
- difficulty answering basic questions about eviction, corruption recovery, or low-storage behavior

## Scope

- define cache tiers and invalidation strategy
- clarify persistent storage direction and migration strategy
- improve schema/versioning expectations
- document or reduce ad hoc dependency/platform decisions
- reduce duplicated “local solution per feature” patterns where a shared strategy is warranted

## Existing Related Work

- `#3624`
- `#3618`
- `#3657`
- `#3635`
- `#3629`
- `#3660`

## Acceptance Criteria

- caching and persistence work is grouped under a coherent parent issue
- the repo has an explicit direction for storage and cache policy
- dependency/platform ownership questions are no longer floating as unrelated audit leaves
- related leaf issues can be closed or superseded into this epic

## Done When

- data foundation work is coordinated instead of fragmented
- storage/cache decisions are easier to reason about and evolve safely
- the highest-value migrations or policy decisions are decomposed into concrete child work

---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. define target storage/cache direction
2. group and supersede related audit leaves
3. sequence migrations and policy decisions by payoff and risk

## Subgroup
- `@NotThatKindOfDrLiz` — DRI
- `@realmeylisdev` — persistence/caching support
- `@untreu2` — data/repository support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a platform or storage decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for data foundation decisions
- separate immediate execution work from long-horizon design questions
- avoid introducing new storage/caching paths without checking against this direction
- prefer explicit policy over one-off per-feature exceptions

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.

issue.title: fix(security): remove BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth PKCE verifier and request body
issue.body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
Critical

## Problem
BYOK registration embeds the user nsec into the PKCE verifier and posts the nsec to Keycast during headless registration.

## Evidence
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart:9-12 appends .$nsec to the PKCE verifier.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:155-171 accepts optional nsec and uses it in verifier generation.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:280-286 derives BYOK pubkey and generates verifier with nsec.
- mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart:299-301 puts nsec into the registration request body.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:81-95 exports local nsec and passes it into registration.
- mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart:117-122 calls headlessRegister(... nsec: nsec ...).

## Impact
BYOK/private key material leaves local storage and is also carried in the PKCE verifier, breaking the expected local-key custody boundary.

## Recommended fix
Never send or embed nsec. Use a local proof-of-possession challenge signed by the key, or send only byok_pubkey and a signature over server-provided nonce/session data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No nsec appears in OAuth URL, PKCE verifier, persisted pending verification, request body, logs, or tests.
- [ ] Server receives only public key plus proof.
- [ ] BYOK registration still binds the account to the intended Nostr pubkey.
- [ ] Tests assert verifier does not contain nsec1.

## Related issues
Adjacent: #969, #3066, #3270.

Negative-regression tests across 4 layers (`pkce_test`, `oauth_client_test` ×2, `secure_account_screen_test` ×3, `pending_verification_service_test` ×3).

`divinevideo/keycast#197` Phase A is concretely scoped (4 acceptance criteria, 3-phase rollout) and **its issue body explicitly designates PR #3784 as "the emergency-block PR that disables the BYOK preservation path entirely" pre-Phase-B**. Phase A acceptance criteria includes graceful migration support — "Continue accepting legacy register shape with deprecation log + Sunset: response header" — meaning the server team has already designed Phase A around this mobile PR landing first.

- **Approach B** (wait for Phase 2): keep #3784 in DRAFT; land combined Phase 1 + Phase 2 PR after keycast#197 ships. issue.title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth wire (#3359)
issue.body:
## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the
server-side proof-of-possession redesign that Phase 2 depends on.
This PR ships **without** preserving BYOK identity binding — that is
restored once Phase 2 lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ❌ Breaking change (the public `KeycastOAuth.headlessRegister` and `KeycastOAuth.getAuthorizationUrl` APIs no longer accept `nsec` — intentional, for security)

## Trade-off

Until Phase 2 ships, BYOK secure-account upgrades fall through to the
server's auto-generate path. The user's existing local pubkey identity
is **not preserved** across the upgrade, but the local nsec stays
on-device and never crosses the network. This is the intentional
emergency-block trade-off — stop the leak today, restore identity
preservation in Phase 2 (depends on divinevideo/keycast#197).

## What's in this PR

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart` | `generateVerifier` no longer takes `nsec`; verifier is always pure-random base64url |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart` | `getAuthorizationUrl` & `headlessRegister` drop `nsec`/`byokPubkey` parameters; `body['nsec']` removed; `byok_pubkey` URL param removed |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/test/{pkce,oauth_client}_test.dart` | Leak-as-feature tests flipped to negative regression guards |
| `mobile/lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart` | `load()` discards any persisted verifier containing `.nsec1` and clears storage (defense-in-depth migration) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Error log no longer interpolates `_pendingVerifier` value |
| `mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart` | Removed `authService.exportNsec()` and the `nsec:` arg |
| `mobile/test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart` | **New** — three tests for the migration |
| `mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` | **New** — POSIX-grep guard for production code |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | New `nsec-leak-guard` job |
| `mobile/integration_test/auth/session_expired_banner_test.dart` | `markTestSkipped` until Phase 2 — depends on BYOK preservation |

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages/keycast_flutter/{lib,test}` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/keycast_flutter/` — 167/167 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart test/screens/auth/secure_account_screen_test.dart test/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit_test.dart` — 38/38 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/divine_auth/` — 64/64 passing (regression-safety on the path that never carried nsec)
- [x] `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` — exits 0 on this branch
- [x] Guard regex verified: matches `body['nsec']` + `'nsec':`; ignores `containsKey('nsec')` + `any(named: 'nsec')`
- [ ] Manual: e2e secure-account upgrade flow on a local dev stack (post-merge or staging)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra/security on retention review for any pre-fix request bodies that infra-layer components may have captured (separate workstream)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- divinevideo/keycast#197 — server-side proof-of-possession contract (Phase 2A)
- A separate Phase 2 mobile PR — restores BYOK identity preservation via the new server contract (depends on keycast#197 being in production)
- Orphaned ARB key `authUnableToAccessKeys` (no longer referenced from Dart) — left in place to avoid touching 16 locale files; safe to remove in a follow-up

## Scope

### 1. Systematic email-PII log redaction (rabble #3784 review item 4, option 2)

The PR's original change at `lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart:113`
followed the established 5-site convention of logging email at info/warning
level in the same auth flow. Rather than redact only the new warning
(creating inconsistency without security benefit), the agreed-upon path
is to address all 6 sites systematically here.

**Sites to redact:**

- `lib/blocs/divine_auth/divine_auth_cubit.dart:275`
- `lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart:75`
- `lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart:68` (`save`)
- `lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart:113` (`load` — Phase 1 migration warning)
- `lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart:144` (`load` — expired/clearing info)
- `lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart:153` (`load` — loaded info)

**Approach:**

- Add `redactEmailForLogs(String email)` colocated with
  `lib/utils/sensitive_uri_for_logs.dart` (existing redaction utility
  surface).
- Apply across the 6 sites.
- Unit tests mirror the shape of
  `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk/test/unit/redact_http_headers_for_logs_test.dart`.

### 2. Orphaned ARB key removal

`authUnableToAccessKeys` is no longer referenced from Dart after
PR #3784 (acknowledged in the PR description as deferred). Remove
across:

- `lib/l10n/app_en.arb` (source of truth)
- `lib/l10n/app_*.arb` (16 translated locales — confirm exact list
  with `ls mobile/lib/l10n/app_*.arb` before editing)
- Regenerate via `flutter gen-l10n` from `mobile/`

### 3. Lessons capture (re-opens #3787 workstream)

Append to `tasks/lessons.md` (or its current equivalent):

> Any function that returns a verifier/token/secret and accepts the
> user's private key material as input is a CI failure. Reading
> `pkce.dart:9 generateVerifier(String nsec)` would have caught
> #3359 a year earlier.

PR #3787 originally filed for this lessons capture; was closed unmerged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 6 email-log sites redact via the new helper
- [ ] Unit tests cover the helper (nsec1, npub1, mixed, none, multiple)
- [ ] `flutter gen-l10n` succeeds with no orphaned-key warnings
- [ ] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` clean
- [ ] `tasks/lessons.md` lesson entry present
- [ ] Existing `divine_auth_cubit_test.dart` redaction-pattern tests
      (lines 535-538) continue to pass

## Out of scope

- The PR #3784 security fix itself (already addresses option 1 of
  rabble's item 4 by matching established convention)
- Phase 2 BYOK identity preservation (#3786, blocked on
  divinevideo/keycast#197)
- Any further PII redaction outside the email-log sites listed above

## Related

- PR #3784 — Phase 1 emergency block (this issue follows up on it)
- #3786 — Phase 2 mobile tracking issue
- divinevideo/keycast#197 — Phase 2 server contract

Please add the tracked TODO here, or remove the fallback if we no longer need to support old tray notifications.

issue.title: epic(testing): reduce skipped coverage debt and stabilize test infrastructure
issue.body:
## Summary

Testing debt is currently spread across skipped tests, missing service coverage, flaky timing patterns, weak integration coverage, and CI enforcement gaps. This needs one parent issue so testing work can be sequenced intentionally instead of living as scattered audit fragments.

This issue is the source of truth for testing and CI debt reduction.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- too many skipped tests with no active execution path
- large service areas with weak or missing direct coverage
- test timing patterns that create flakiness or overhead
- insufficient integration coverage for important runtime flows
- CI coverage policy that is still inconsistent across scopes

## Scope

- reduce skipped test debt
- improve direct coverage for untested services and flows
- replace timing-based test patterns where appropriate
- restore or retire stale test suites intentionally
- tighten CI coverage expectations where it improves signal

## Existing Related Work

- `#3608`
- `#3609`
- `#3610`
- `#3612`
- `#3614`
- `#3616`
- `#3576`
- `#3577`

## Acceptance Criteria

- major testing debt categories are coordinated under one parent issue
- skipped/untested/flaky/CI coverage work has a clear execution home
- related audit leaves can be closed or superseded into this epic
- future test cleanup work has an obvious place to land

## Done When

- testing debt is organized into a manageable execution model
- the repo has fewer ambiguous “someday test cleanup” issues
- the highest-value testing improvements are decomposed into concrete child work

---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. define triage policy for skipped and stale tests
2. group and supersede scattered testing audit leaves
3. execute the highest-signal coverage and infrastructure fixes first

## Subgroup
- `@NotThatKindOfDrLiz` — DRI
- `@realmeylisdev` — CI/test execution support
- `@untreu2` — coverage and test cleanup support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a testing policy decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for testing debt cleanup
- prefer meaningful signal over raw test count growth
- delete or retire dead/low-value tests when that is the right outcome
- avoid preserving stale test debt just because it already exists

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.
